claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm looking to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one son, Alex.

To help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to gather some details about your circumstances.

**What is Alex's date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 16 years old - just turned 16 a few months ago.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. So Alex is 16 years old and turned 16 a few months ago.

**Are you a UK resident, and do you have parental responsibility for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and Alex lives here with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, thank you for confirming that. I have a few more questions to complete the assessment.

**What is your current employment or education status? For example, are you working, self-employed, unemployed, or in full-time education?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm working - I have a regular job. But I think you need to know more about Alex's situation rather than mine, right?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're absolutely right, and I appreciate you pointing that out! Let me focus on Alex's circumstances now.

**Is Alex currently in full-time education, training, or apprenticeship?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's in full-time education - he's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's very helpful.

**Does Alex receive any income or benefits in his own right, such as Disability Living Allowance, Personal Independence Payment, or other state benefits?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

**Is there anyone else who is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has Alex been claimed for by another person?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for that confirmation.

I now have sufficient information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex. Let me review the circumstances:

- Alex is 16 years old and turned 16 a few months ago
- Alex is in full-time education (A-levels at sixth form college)
- Alex does not receive any state benefits in his own name
- You have parental responsibility and Alex lives with you in the UK
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

Based on the Child Benefit eligibility rules, children can be eligible up to age 19 if they are in full-time education or approved training. Since Alex is 16, in full-time education, and meets all the other criteria, you should be eligible to claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent news! **You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Alex meets all the requirements because:
- He is 16 years old and in full-time education (studying A-levels)
- Child Benefit extends to age 19 for children in full-time education
- He lives with you in the UK where you have parental responsibility
- He does not receive any state benefits in his own name
- No one else is claiming for him

If you haven't already done so, you can apply for Child Benefit through the official UK government channels. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
